Description: They set the overall vision and strategic direction, guiding the vision and planning process. They are responsible for approving, endorsing and owning the national eHealth vision and carrying out strategic recommendations.
Examples:
National eHealth steering committee
Other government committees or councils to which the steering committee reports (e.g. the steering committee may be a subset of a broader health and/or ICT council).

Description: They are not involved directly in decision-making but are highly influential in decisions relating to the national eHealth vision. This is due to their acknowledged eminence and expertise in the field; and their role as formal or informal advisers to key decision-makers.
Examples:
Senior executives in key health organizations
Senior executives in funding and investment organizations
Eminent academics and experts
Other advisers to steering committee members and other relevant government committees and councils

Description: They are not involved in, nor have influence on, decision-making, but are a source of subject matter expertise. They have a strong interest in the national eHealth vision because of the impact it will have on them and/or their organization.
Examples:
Members of advocacy groups (e.g. privacy, public, vendors, industry, unions, etc.)
Patient associations and advocacy groups
Health agency executives (e.g. NGOs, hospitals, etc.)
Health committees and programmes

Description:
There may be sections of the general public who are aware of developments in eHealth and are interested in the potential impacts on them.
There may also be a requirement to ask the general public to provide input or endorsement of components of the national eHealth vision.
